families.rule: Guten + time of day = a greeting.

pair.note: Nacht is a die-word: gute, not guten. And it means goodbye, not hello.

families.rule: Wie geht's? is the everyday “How are you?”
Ich bin ___ = I am ___. No “a” before a job: Ich bin Student.

pair.note: A yes/no question starts with the verb.

families.rule: heißen = to be called. du heißt, Sie heißen (polite).

pair.note: Sie is the polite “you”, and the verb ending changes with it.

families.rule: aus + place = from. Woher = where from.

pair.note: du → kommst, Sie → kommen.

families.rule: Bis + a time = see you then.
Das ist + a describing word = That's ___.

pair.note: nicht goes before the describing word.

families.rule: sprechen = to speak. Sprechen Sie ___? asks politely.

pair.note: The question puts the verb first.

families.rule: Ich hätte gern + a thing = the polite “I'd like”.

pair.note: Kaffee is a der-word → einen. Wasser is a das-word → ein.

families.rule: möchte = would like. A second verb goes to the very end.

sentences.en: I'd like to drink a coffee.

pair.note: Add a second verb and it goes to the end.

families.rule: Thing + bitte is enough to order.
Haben Sie ___? = Do you have ___? The verb comes first.

sentences.en: Do you have a free table?

families.rule: Kann ich + … + verb at the end = Can I …?

pair.note: Only the way of paying changes; zahlen stays at the end.

families.rule: Wo ist ___? Learn each noun with der, die or das.
After suche, der becomes den. die and das stay the same.

sentences.en: I'm looking for the train station.

pair.note: der → den after suche. die and das don't change.
halb vier is half TO four: 3:30.

families.rule: German “has” hunger and thirst: Ich habe Hunger = I'm hungry.

pair.note: Tired uses bin; hungry and thirsty use habe.

families.rule: mein for der- and das-words, meine for die-words.

pair.note: Schwester is a die-word → meine.

families.rule: Age uses bin: Ich bin 20 Jahre alt.
verb + gern = I like doing it.

pair.note: gern turns “I drink” into “I like drinking”.

families.rule: mögen = to like (a thing). kein/keinen = not any.

pair.note: keinen, not nicht, before a noun.

families.rule: Weather uses es: Es ist kalt. Es regnet.

sentences.en: When does the next bus leave?

families.rule: brauchen = to need. der-words take einen: einen Arzt.
Pain and fever use habe: Ich habe Fieber.
Question words come first: was, wer, wann, warum.
Hast du Zeit? = Are you free?
gehen = to go (on foot, or in general).
arbeiten = to work. als + job = as a …

sentences.en: What do you do for a living?

families.rule: Es gibt = there is / there are.
Wie sagt man … auf Deutsch? = How do you say … in German?

sentences.en: How do you say “bill” in German?

families.rule: Say how well you speak: Ich lerne / spreche / verstehe …
Das macht … = That comes to … (the total).

sentences.en: That comes to a hundred euros.

pair.note: German says the ones first: zwei-und-zwanzig, “two and twenty”.

families.rule: Phone numbers are read digit by digit or in pairs.

sentences.de: Meine Nummer ist [null eins sieben drei].
sentences.en: My number is zero one seven three.

families.rule: Days are der-words: der Montag, am Montag = on Monday.
Buying food: a quantity + the thing.

sentences.en: I'd like a loaf of bread.
I'd like a kilo of apples.
alt: Ich hätte gerne ein Kilo Äpfel.

sentences.en: I'd like two hundred grams of cheese.
alt: Ich hätte gerne zweihundert Gramm Käse.

families.rule: Wo finde ich …? = Where can I find …?

sentences.en: Where are the fruit and vegetables?
Do you have it in a smaller size?

families.rule: Colours come after ist without an ending.

sentences.en: Do you have a room available?

families.rule: Wann gibt es …? = When is … served?
Asking for things at the table.
Mir ist … = I feel … (a set phrase).

pair.note: Feeling cold or sick uses mir ist, not ich bin.

families.rule: Wo ist hier …? = Where is there a … around here?

sentences.en: Is there a supermarket around here?
Is there a bank around here?
Is there a cash machine around here?
Is there a restaurant around here?

families.rule: Wie komme ich zum/zur …? = How do I get to …?

sentences.en: How do I get to the station?
How do I get to the post office?
How do I get to the airport?
How do I get to the centre?

pair.note: zum for der- and das-words, zur for die-words.

sentences.en: The first street on the left.
The second street on the right.

families.rule: nehmen = to take (a bus, a taxi).

sentences.en: Where do I buy a ticket?
Where do I have to get off?

families.rule: Talking about family: Ich habe + einen/eine/ein.
du-forms end in -st: du wohnst, du arbeitest.

pair.note: ich → -e, du → -st.

families.rule: er, sie and es forms end in -t: er wohnt, sie arbeitet.
wir and Sie use the dictionary form: wir wohnen, Sie wohnen.
ihr = you (several people you know well); ends in -t.
sein (to be) is irregular: ich bin, du bist, er ist, wir sind, ihr seid, sie sind.
haben (to have): ich habe, du hast, er hat, wir haben.
The verb is always second: a time word first, then the verb, then ich.

sentences.en: Today I'm going to the cinema.

pair.note: Start with the time, and the verb still comes second: ich moves behind it.

sentences.en: At the weekend we're going to the sea.
In summer we travel a lot.
After the meal we drink coffee.
After that we go for a walk.

families.rule: wohin = where to; wo = where (no movement).

sentences.en: Where are you going on holiday?

pair.note: wo for where something is, wohin for where it is going.

families.rule: Wie viel for amounts, wie viele for things you count.

sentences.en: How much time do you have?
How many children do you have?
How much money do you need?
How long have you been learning German?

families.rule: Wie + describing word asks for a quality.

sentences.en: How far is it to the station?
Which bus goes to the centre?

families.rule: Yes/no questions start with the verb.
können = can. The second verb goes to the end.

pair.note: With können, the other verb moves to the end in its dictionary form.

sentences.en: Do you have to work tomorrow?
We have to get up early.

families.rule: wollen = want to. ich will, du willst, er will.

sentences.en: Do you want to come along?
He wants to buy a car.
We want to go to Berlin.
You're not allowed to park here.
May I interrupt for a moment?
You're supposed to call the doctor.

families.rule: möchte + verb at the end = would like to.

sentences.en: I'd like to book a room.
I'd like to make an appointment.

families.rule: der-words take den/einen after most verbs (accusative).

pair.note: As the thing you buy or see, der becomes den.

families.rule: kein/keine/keinen = no, not any (before a noun).

sentences.en: She has no brothers or sisters.

families.rule: nicht negates a verb, describing word or whole idea.

pair.note: kein before a noun on its own, nicht for everything else.

sentences.en: I get up at seven o'clock.
On Sunday I get up late.

families.rule: anrufen splits: Ich rufe dich an.

sentences.en: Where do you do your shopping?
We do the shopping on Saturday.
I still have to do the shopping.

pair.note: After muss, the split verb joins up again at the end.

families.rule: mitkommen / mitnehmen: mit goes to the end.

sentences.en: Are you taking that with you?

families.rule: anfangen = to begin; aufhören = to stop.

sentences.en: I watch TV in the evening.
The children watch too much TV.

families.rule: ankommen = to arrive; abfahren = to leave.

sentences.en: Will you pick me up from the station?

sentences.de: [Um acht Uhr] fahre ich zur Arbeit.
sentences.en: At eight o'clock I go to work.

sentences.de: Um [halb sechs] komme ich nach Hause.
sentences.en: At half past five I come home.
At eleven I go to bed.
In the morning I drink coffee.

families.rule: How often: immer, oft, manchmal, selten, nie.

sentences.en: I sometimes go to the cinema.

families.rule: Some verbs change their vowel with du and er: fahren → du fährst, er fährt.

sentences.en: She reads the paper every day.
She takes sugar in her tea.

families.rule: wissen = to know (a fact): ich weiß, du weißt, er weiß.

pair.note: kennen for people and places, wissen for facts.

sentences.en: Will you pass me the salt?

families.rule: lieber = rather, prefer; am liebsten = most of all.

sentences.en: Most of all I like eating pasta.
What do you like doing most?

pair.note: gern → lieber → am liebsten: like → prefer → like most.

sentences.en: My hobbies are sport and music.
In my free time I take photos.
What do you do in your free time?

families.rule: in einer Wohnung (die), in einem Haus (das).

sentences.en: I live on the third floor.
The flat has a big kitchen.

families.rule: Furniture: der Tisch, die Lampe, das Sofa.

sentences.en: Can you take out the rubbish, please?
Can you turn off the light, please?
Can you close the door, please?
Can you do the washing-up, please?

families.rule: dein/deine = your (to someone you say du to).

pair.note: The word depends on the owner: his car = sein Auto, her car = ihr Auto.

families.rule: unser = our, euer = your (several people), Ihr = your (polite).
Plurals have many endings; learn each with die.
In the plural, der, die and das all become die.
Hair and eyes: Sie hat … Haare, … Augen.
tragen = to wear; du trägst, er trägt.

sentences.en: We've been together for five years.
My baby is three months old.
Do you have this in size M?
Do you have this in black?

pair.note: One thing tut weh, several things tun weh.

sentences.en: I need tablets for a headache.

families.rule: seit + time = for (and still going on).

sentences.en: I've had a fever since yesterday.
I've been ill for three days.
I've had a cough for a week.

sentences.de: Seit [heute Morgen] tut mein Bauch weh.
sentences.en: My stomach has hurt since this morning.

families.rule: Meals: das Frühstück, das Mittagessen, das Abendessen.

sentences.de: Zum Abendessen essen wir [Brot mit Käse].
sentences.en: For dinner we eat bread and cheese.
Would you like to try it?

families.rule: kostet for one thing, kosten for several.

sentences.en: Can I pay with my phone?

families.rule: Dates: der erste, der zweite, der dritte …

sentences.en: Today is the first of March.
Today is the twelfth of June.
My birthday is on the third of October.

families.rule: Time words: diese Woche, nächste Woche.

sentences.en: This week I'm working a lot.
I go swimming once a week.

families.rule: Polite commands: verb first, then Sie.
Accusative pronouns: mich, dich, ihn, sie, es, uns, euch.

pair.note: er becomes ihn when he is the one you like or see.

families.rule: für + accusative: für mich, für dich, für ihn.

sentences.en: I'm buying this for my father.
We have a present for you.
Without glasses I can't see anything.

families.rule: Es gibt + accusative: es gibt einen Park.
Jobs: no “a” in German. Female forms often end in -in.

sentences.en: I work from nine to five.
I have the day off today.
I have a lot to do today.
I'm on the late shift today.

sentences.de: Ich habe [eine Frage] zu Seite zehn.
sentences.en: I have a question about page ten.
Can I speak to Mr Weber?
Can you speak a bit louder?

families.rule: Lust haben auf = to feel like.

sentences.en: Shall we meet in front of the cinema?

families.rule: einladen = to invite; also: to treat.

sentences.de: Ich lade dich [zu meiner Party] ein.
sentences.en: I'm inviting you to my party.

families.rule: mit + dem/der: mit dem Bus, mit der Bahn.
und, aber, oder, denn don't change the word order.

sentences.de: Ich bin müde, [aber] ich arbeite noch.
sentences.en: I'm tired, but I'm still working.

sentences.de: Ich trinke Kaffee [und] esse ein Brötchen.
sentences.en: I drink coffee and eat a roll.
Would you like tea or coffee?

sentences.de: Ich bleibe zu Hause, [denn] ich bin krank.
sentences.en: I'm staying at home because I'm ill.
I'm not coming today but tomorrow.
He isn't a teacher but a doctor.

sentences.de: Wir fahren nicht mit dem Auto, [sondern mit dem Zug].
sentences.en: We're not going by car but by train.

families.rule: Order of events: zuerst, dann, danach, zum Schluss.
schon = already; noch = still; noch nicht = not yet.

sentences.en: I've lived here for a long time.
How do you write your name?

families.rule: nach Hause = (going) home; zu Hause = at home.

pair.note: zu Hause for where you are, nach Hause for where you're going.

families.rule: durch = through, um = around, gegen = against (+ accusative).
finden = to find, to think (an opinion).

sentences.en: What do you think of it?

families.rule: erklären = to explain; zeigen = to show.

sentences.en: Can you explain that to me?
Can you show me the way?

families.rule: bringen = to bring; schicken = to send.

sentences.en: Can you bring me the book?
How long have you been waiting?
I'm listening to a podcast in German.

sentences.de: In der Stadt gibt es [ein Museum].
sentences.en: There's a museum in the town.
The supermarket is open until ten.
I'd like to open an account.
I'd like to change money into euros.
I'd like to send a parcel.

sentences.de: Ich möchte [einen Brief] nach Ägypten schicken.
sentences.en: I'd like to send a letter to Egypt.
How long does the letter take?
I have an appointment at the authorities' office.
I was born on the fifth of May.
Can you send me the link?
Can you send me your address?
I'm going on holiday to Spain.
Do you have a table for two?
Excuse me, what time is it?
Excuse me, is this your seat?
Excuse me, may I get past?
Excuse me, do you speak English?
The house is a hundred years old.
